_comment: The CLOSED capability registry (ADR-0562). The single machine-readable source of truth for the canonical capability set of the capability-first repo organization. Coarse / Conway-aligned: one capability per two-pizza ownership boundary. Seeded from ADR-0536's sixteen substrate domains + the verified current tree (cloud/ + oya/). A crate maps to EXACTLY ONE registered capability via the ADR-0562 deterministic placement rule; new top-level dirs outside this registry plus base/build/governance/kernel/os/app FAIL the membership lint. De-brand naming is realized via the ADR-0532/0533 profile mechanism; the names here are the de-branded canonical slugs (the flip is a later Phase-0 lane). This file is governance data; its eventual home is governance/capability-registry.json after the reorg, held at specs/ until the governance/ top-level dir is created. DATA, not code: canonical-json governed, reachability-registered, council-architecture owned.

meta_directories.charter: kuberos no_std kernel + sysroot; the recursion floor. Its own excluded/nested workspace per the ADR-0512 kernel carve-out.
cloud-os node operating system (Talos-class). The node substrate the capability ladder runs on.

Irreducible cross-capability primitives (Google //base). Admission rule: a crate enters base/ ONLY if depended-on by >=3 capabilities AND strictly below all of them in the ADR-0280 DAG. NOT a util/ junk-drawer.
Meta, off the runtime ladder: ADRs, specs, policy-as-data, this capability registry, the dep-lint authority, the masterplan.
Meta, off the runtime ladder: buck2 prelude, toolchains, reindeer, third_party vendoring, CI engines, and the generated sell-catalog (SKU/pricing) VIEW. Owns zero capability crates.
Composition ring: deployable surfaces wiring 2+ capabilities for a tenant (SaaS verticals + the web shell). app/<product>/ composes; it never defines a capability engine.

faces.charter: Capability traits; the stable seam. The lowest ADR-0280 DAG node the crate's public port belongs to is the tie-breaker for placement.
Transient-infra impls (adapter-aws/-oci/-capi); vanish at owned-stack cutover.
The multi-tenant surface we SELL (product face); depends on core/ ONLY through ports.

capabilities.name: cell
capabilities.charter: Cellular topology substrate: cluster-per-cell, hard caps, thin static-stable cell router, autosharding/rebalancing. The leaf substrate (ADR-0280 bootstrap floor).

capabilities.name: iam
capabilities.charter: Identity + authorization: IdP (principals/credentials/passkeys), product-shared identity, consent, tenant-RBAC, and the embedded Cedar PDP + policy store. Cross-cutting authz spectrum RBAC+ABAC+PBAC.
capabilities.boundary_note: Coarse collapse per founder ruling: identity + oya-identity + consent(-graph) + tenant-rbac + policy as sub-modules of iam. The cloud IdP substrate and the product-shared identity that CONSUMES it are sub-modules with distinct faces (core vs facade), not separate capabilities.

capabilities.name: tenancy
capabilities.charter: Tenant lifecycle + home-cell resolution + tenant-as-universal-scoping-primitive. The structural multi-tenancy substrate.

capabilities.name: secrets
capabilities.charter: KMS + secrets + workload identity (SPIFFE/SVID issuance). The crypto root (recursion break #1).
capabilities.boundary_note: KMS (key material) and secrets (secret material) share an OWNERS boundary and the crypto-root recursion break; kept coarse. Workload-identity SVID issuance (ADR-0553/0561) lives here as the issuance engine; consuming PEPs live in iam/.

capabilities.name: audit
capabilities.charter: Tamper-evident Merkle audit log; always-on, no kill switch. Seals the emitting principal + tenant scope.

capabilities.name: observability
capabilities.charter: Metrics/logs/traces/SLO substrate (ADR-0139 SLO-gated promotion). The agentic observability plane.

capabilities.name: data
capabilities.charter: Data substrate: ontology graph, OLTP/OLAP storage engines, pipelines/warehouse, replication/residency. The owned data plane.

capabilities.name: storage
capabilities.charter: Object/blob storage + content-addressed store (CAS / NativeLink). Crypto-shred-aware blob substrate.
capabilities.boundary_note: FLAGGED for leader: storage (substrate CAS/blob) vs data (ontology/OLTP) is a clean port seam, but the consumer-facing drive/imaging/recordings facades could alternatively be modeled as app/ verticals. Kept under storage/facade pending OWNERS confirmation.

capabilities.name: compute
capabilities.charter: ONE compute engine: VM + k8s-on-compute + functions/serverless, with facade sub-surfaces. The owned compute plane.
capabilities.boundary_note: Coarse per founder ruling: compute is ONE engine (vm + k8s-on-compute + functions) with facade sub-surfaces, NOT three capabilities.

capabilities.name: k8s
capabilities.charter: Owned Kubernetes control plane (core) + managed-k8s product (facade). kuberos->cloud-k8s ladder rung above os/.
capabilities.boundary_note: Coarse collapse per founder ruling: owned control-plane (core) + managed-k8s (facade). The four managed-k8s-* dirs become facade sub-modules.

capabilities.name: network
capabilities.charter: Network + DNS substrate: service mesh, static-stable signed DNS snapshots, cell routing data plane.

capabilities.name: gateway
capabilities.charter: API gateway / SSOT edge: Check/Report enforcement point, public API contract surface, rate/quota enforcement.

capabilities.name: messaging
capabilities.charter: Event bus / messaging substrate (Pulsar/Oxia transient -> owned Rust destination): idempotency, outbox, backpressure, per-key ordering.

capabilities.name: intelligence
capabilities.charter: AI/intelligence substrate: SDK adapters, request pipeline + proof layer, agentic capabilities. cloud-intelligence destination.

capabilities.name: workflow
capabilities.charter: Orchestration substrate: workflow engine + studio. Cross-capability composition via events.

capabilities.name: ci
capabilities.charter: The delivery fabric: cloud-ci gates, controller, Tide merge queue, webhook gateway, the pipeline-as-product paved road. ADR-0515/0548.
capabilities.boundary_note: Coarse collapse per founder ruling: ci absorbs cloud-ci + ci-controller + ci-tide + ci-webhook-gateway as sub-modules.

capabilities.name: iac
capabilities.charter: Infrastructure-as-code substrate + GitOps reconciliation surfaces. Declarative state for the owned stack.

capabilities.name: billing
capabilities.charter: Metering + billing + pricing: three-clock accrual/rating/invoicing, tax, FinOps cost attribution. First-class sold-ness capability (NOT a product/ junk-drawer).
capabilities.boundary_note: Coarse collapse: metering + billing + tax + finops/cost as sub-modules. First-class cross-cutting sold-ness capability per founder ruling.

capabilities.name: marketplace
capabilities.charter: Marketplace + plugin/app store + SKU catalog data. First-class cross-cutting sold-ness capability.
capabilities.boundary_note: First-class sold-ness capability per founder ruling. The generated SKU/pricing sell-catalog VIEW is materialized as build/ output over face:facade crates; marketplace owns the marketplace ENGINE, not the catalog view.

capabilities.name: console
capabilities.charter: Operator/tenant console shell: one platform-owned Leptos shell composed at build time; sole token broker; replaces all operator CLIs.
capabilities.boundary_note: FLAGGED for leader: the console SHELL is substrate (capability); the per-product surfaces that compile INTO it are app/<product>/ composition members. The boundary between console/core (shell + token broker) and app/ surfaces needs OWNERS confirmation.

capabilities.name: compliance
capabilities.charter: Compliance + governance evidence substrate: regulatory packs, data-class registry, DPIA/threat-model evidence, audit-pack generation.
capabilities.boundary_note: FLAGGED for leader: compliance (regulatory evidence) is distinguished from audit (tamper-evident log) by a clean port seam, but they share heavy coupling; a future amendment may collapse them. Kept separate pending OWNERS.

capabilities.name: comms
capabilities.charter: Communications substrate: email/mail, messenger, meet, notifications, contact-center. Multi-channel comms plane.
capabilities.boundary_note: FLAGGED for leader: comms is a sold product family AND a substrate (notifications). The substrate notification engine is core/; messenger/meet/mail tenant surfaces may belong in app/ instead. Needs OWNERS confirmation.

capabilities.name: flags
capabilities.charter: Feature-flag / configuration substrate: dynamic config, progressive delivery, kill switches.

app_products_note: Deployable SaaS verticals (crm, hr, healthcare/emr/pharmacy/patient-monitoring/imaging, itsm, incident-management, payroll, treasury, payments, supply-chain-planning, production-planning, plant-maintenance, warehouse, real-estate, global-trade, learning-management, performance-management, quality-management, contract-lifecycle-management, financial-planning, marketing-automation, social, community, connect, office/docs/sheets/slides/notes/sites/whiteboard/calendar/forms/design-collaboration, translate, etc.) are app/<product>/ composition members under the placement rule, NOT capabilities. They wire 2+ capabilities for a tenant. The exact app/ roster is enumerated by the migration lanes, not closed here; this registry closes the CAPABILITY axis only.
flagged_boundaries_for_leader: storage vs data facades (drive/imaging/recordings): capability facade or app vertical?
console shell vs app/<product> surfaces that compile into it: where is the shell/surface line?
compliance vs audit: clean port seam exists, heavy coupling; collapse candidate.
comms substrate notifications vs comms product surfaces (messenger/meet/mail): substrate or app?

intelligence/workflow/iac/tenancy dag_node reconciliation (RESOLVED in Phase-0 when specs/substrate-dependency-dag.json was populated to ADR-0280 §D-1 verbatim): tenancy, intelligence, and workflow-engine ARE present in the §D-1 Tier-1 ten (this flag predated reading §D-1, which already carries them) — their dag_node names are confirmed canonical. The fourth, iac (dag_node 'iac'; ADR-0280 Appendix C names it 'cloud-iac', tier_subtype substrate-iac), is a TIER-2 substrate forward-declared per ADR-0280 Appendix C and lands in DAG v1.1.0, NOT the v1.0.0 Tier-1 file. See the substrate-dependency-dag.json _comment for the full reconciliation.

membership_lint_coverage._comment: ADR-0562 §6 membership-lint COVERAGE extension (Phase-0). The capabilities[].absorbs_current_dirs close the cloud/+oya/ SERVICE-dir axis; this block extends the closed registry to map EVERY remaining current crate (the cloud/oya app surfaces with no capability service-dir, plus the libs/ and tools/ crates that dissolve into capability homes + meta dirs per ADR-0562 §1, 'libs/ dissolves into capability homes + base/'). Each entry maps a PRE-MOVE current path → a registered capability slug OR a meta directory (kernel/os/base/governance/build/app). The membership lint reads these PRE-MOVE; POST-move the path itself is the namespace. Genuinely-ambiguous crates that the strangler must home per-crate are NOT force-mapped here — they live in frozen_unmapped_baseline and the gate enforces no-regression against that frozen set. DATA, not code.

app_products._comment: The cloud/+oya/ deployable SaaS verticals + the web/application shell that are app/<product>/ composition members (app_products_note made machine-readable). They wire 2+ capabilities for a tenant and define no capability engine. PRE-MOVE these live at oya/<product>/; POST-move at app/<product>/. workplace-integration is the 'etc.' catch-all surface in app_products_note. application is the developer application/web shell (product-developer-application-shell) that compiles INTO the console capability per the console boundary_note → app/.

meta_directory_absorbs._comment: kuberos kernel + sysroot floor (ADR-0512 carve-out). cloud-kernel is the single 2nd-level crate.

absorbs_current_crate_globs._comment: The dep-lint / check authority + the governance kernels + the corpus substrate. ADR-0562 §1 names 'the dep-lint authority' as a governance/ resident; owns_crates:false on the meta dir means it owns no CAPABILITY crates, not that governance/ hosts no governance-engine code (consistent with build/'s 'Owns zero capability crates' wording). The libs/oya-check-* and libs/oya-governance-* crates ARE the dep-lint authority; ADR-0580's governance/corpus/* crates (corpus-core, corpus-extract) are the Phase -1 live-AST corpus substrate physically homed under governance/ — also governance-engine code, not a capability crate. The membership-lint glob is a stem starts_with match, so governance/corpus/* covers both leaves.

Off-runtime-ladder build/CI engines + buck2/workspace/manifest-generation tooling. ADR-0562 §1 build/ charter: 'buck2 prelude, toolchains, reindeer, third_party vendoring, CI engines'. The remaining tools/*-app crates are build/CI tooling, not capability engines.
The owned data plane primitives (ADR-0562 'data→data'): the data boundary/outbox/SQL kernels + adapters dissolve into the data capability home.

The event-bus / messaging substrate primitives dissolve into the messaging capability home (ADR-0280 messaging node; bus/queue/stream boundary kernels are the per-key-ordering/backpressure seam). The substrate-kernel FLOOR has landed at messaging/core/substrate-kernel (de-brand strangler MOVE-1, ADR-0562/0532/0533) — self-owned by the messaging capability dir, so its libs/ membership glob is retired.

frozen_unmapped_baseline._comment: BORN-ADVISORY FROZEN BASELINE (ADR-0562 §6 strangler burn-down). These current crates are genuinely ambiguous PRE-MOVE — they are the libs/oya-shared-* cross-capability junk-drawer the reorg explicitly dissolves PER-CRATE (idempotency/outbox/pagination/pdp/scim/webauthn/etc. each home to a different capability or to base/ pending the >=3-consumer admission check), the libs/oya-http-* middleware (base/ candidates pending the ADR-0280 DAG admission verification), and the irreducible primitives (json) that are base/ candidates. They are NOT force-mapped to a wrong capability. The membership lint is ADVISORY for these but enforces NO REGRESSION: no NEW crate may join this list, no NEW top-level dir may appear, and the list burns DOWN as the strangler moves home each crate. FLIP-TO-BLOCKING TRIGGER: when this list reaches size 0 (post-strangler), the lint promotes from born-advisory to blocking. Each entry is a current crate dir (repo-relative).
